<!--
============================================================================
 READ FIRST. These are hard rules, and CI enforces them (pr-hygiene.yml).
============================================================================

 1. NO AI ATTRIBUTION, anywhere: not in the title, the body, or any commit.
      - no "Co-authored-by:" trailers naming an AI tool or bot e-mail
      - no "Generated with ..." / "Generated by ..." lines
      - no robot-emoji "generated" lines
    The "PR has no AI attribution" job runs scripts/git/check-ai-attribution.sh
    and fails the PR when it finds any of these. You own the change, so you sign it.

 2. TITLE = Conventional Commit, lowercase subject, imperative mood:
      type(scope)?: subject
    Allowed types: feat fix docs style refactor perf test build ci chore revert
    Examples:
      feat(identity): add owner sign-up with 30-day trial
      fix(identity): reject duplicate e-mail on registration
      refactor(platform): extract clock abstraction into shared kernel
      ci: cache nuget packages between jobs
    Rejected: "Feat: Add signup", "fix: Fixed stuff", "WIP".

 3. WRITE IN ENGLISH. Tell a story, not a changelog. Avoid emojis.

 4. Every instruction lives in an HTML comment like this one, so it never
    renders. Replace the placeholders and delete any optional section that
    does not apply. Leave the comments in place: they are invisible.

 Labels: the type:* and module:/area:* labels are applied automatically.
 Add "breaking" yourself if the change breaks a public contract.
============================================================================
-->

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests added or updated, and `just test` passes locally
- [ ] Docs or README updated where behavior or setup changed
- [ ] Analyzers and formatting clean (`just lint`), with no new warnings suppressed
- [ ] Title is a Conventional Commit with a lowercase subject
- [ ] `breaking` label added if a public contract breaks (type/module labels are automatic)
- [ ] No AI attribution in the title, body, or commits
